subject: One-time credit-card payment allowance for 30-day pilot - vendor onboarding

Subject: Quick ask — CC payment for 30-day pilot to avoid PO delay

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for approving the technical kickoff for our 30-day pilot. We can start tomorrow, but our corporate procurement requires a signed PO to set up net-30 invoicing. For a short pilot (estimated spend ~$1,400) the PO cycle will add 10-14 business days, which would delay the program and our mutual evaluation.

Would Redwood consider a one-time credit-card payment option for the pilot so we can begin immediately and still provide procurement the paperwork in parallel? We can provide the onboarding form, W9, and COI up front. If helpful, we can accept a capped credit-card authorization (no charge beyond $2,000 unless pre-approved).

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (stated), sample-insurance.pdf (we'll follow up with full proof).

Appreciate a quick read — Alex and I are flexible on any guardrails you need.

Best,
Elena
Head of Partnerships
EdgeComms AI

Subject: Re: Quick ask — CC payment for 30-day pilot to avoid PO delay

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the proposed cap. Short answer: we can evaluate a one-time credit-card path for pilots when the dollar amount and risk controls are acceptable. I'll need procurement and finance to sign off on conditions.

Next steps from our side:
- Can you attach the completed vendor_onboarding_form and W9 (if not already sent)?
- Please confirm legal entity name and billing address exactly as it should appear on the card receipt.
- We'll run a quick risk check (past disputes, sanctions screening) — should be fine for a public startup like EdgeComms, but we confirm.

Looping in Markus (Finance) and Vanessa (Procurement) to propose guardrails and any paperwork needed. If we agree, I'll approve a one-time CC authorization and mark this pilot as "card-allowed" in the onboarding system.

I'll aim to get a decision by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 11:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — CC payment for 30-day pilot to avoid PO delay

Thanks for the tag. I have a few constraints from finance:

1) Hard cap at $2,000 for non-PO CC authorizations (all mid-size pilots should fit).
2) Require W9 or equivalent tax form, and proof of COI showing at least $1M general liability.
3) Card-allowed pilots must be marked in the ledger as "one-time CC - pilot" so we don't accidentally route renewals through the same channel.
4) We need a short approval email thread saved in the vendor record; procurement will attach a cc_policy_addendum.docx specifying the expiration (30 days) and that any subsequent work requires a PO.

If Procurement (Vanessa) confirms the addendum is acceptable, I can enable the CC route and advise Treasury to accept authorization via Redwood's merchant connector.

Markus
Director, Finance
